description: Unauthorized Access to Cache Data via Transit Gateway Transit Gateway misconfiguration or compromise could allow attackers to intercept or modify cache data flowing between regions, potentially leading to data leakage or tampering. An attacker who gains access to the Transit Gateway's route tables could potentially redirect traffic to malicious endpoints or intercept cross-region cache synchronization data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1210 - Exploitation of Remote Services
recommendation: Implement strict Transit Gateway route table controls

description: Cache Data Leakage Through Misconfigured ElastiCache Security Groups Overly permissive security group rules could allow unauthorized EC2 instances or external actors to connect to ElastiCache clusters. An attacker who compromises an EC2 instance in one VPC might be able to access ElastiCache clusters in another VPC or region if security groups are not properly configured.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict security group rules

description: Cache Poisoning via CloudFront Attackers could potentially inject malicious content into the CloudFront cache by exploiting cache key manipulation or response header manipulation. An attacker could manipulate cache keys or headers to cause CloudFront to cache and serve malicious content to subsequent users requesting the same resource.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service

description: Race Conditions in Cache Rollback Operations Concurrent rollback operations across regions could lead to inconsistent cache states if proper synchronization mechanisms are not in place. During a rollback operation, simultaneous updates to cache clusters in different regions could result in data inconsistency or loss.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: DNS-Based Cache Overload Attackers could exploit DNS misconfigurations to direct excessive traffic to cache clusters, potentially overwhelming them. An attacker could manipulate DNS queries to flood cache clusters with requests, causing service degradation.
references: recommendation: Configure DNS query rate limiting

description: Insecure TLS Configuration in Load Balancers Weak TLS configurations or outdated protocols could allow attackers to intercept or modify traffic between clients and application servers. An attacker performing a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit weak TLS configurations to intercept sensitive data.

Cross-Region Data Leakage Insufficient isolation between regions could allow data to leak across regional boundaries or enable unauthorized access to cache data from different regions. An attacker who compromises one region's resources could potentially access or modify cache data in other regions due to improper isolation.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
